instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a digital delay line. 
A digital delay line is a type of digital circuit that is used to delay a digital signal by a specific amount of time. 
Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a single digital signal (in)
Outputs: a delayed version of the input signal (out)
The module should also have the following parameters:

d: the number of clock cycles by which the signal should be delayed
Your module should implement the following functionality:

The circuit should have a shift register with d stages.
The input signal should be shifted into the first stage of the shift register on each clock cycle.
The output signal should be the value of the signal at the d-th stage of the shift register.
To implement the digital delay line, you should use Verilog code to define the shift register as a set of flip-flops. 
You should then use these flip-flops to shift the input signal into the shift register and to output the delayed signal from the d-th flip-flop.
